2 Has RTE given a written preliminary feasibility letter for at least 500 MW within 36 months at the lead node, with curtailment at or below 10%, and a documented path to more than ~1 GW cumulative hosting in any topology? Written letter for at least 500 MW within 36 months by Month 6. Curtailment target at most 10% (walk-away 15%). Stack of EUR 1.55B-4.2B plus outside-stack lines of EUR 0.5B-1.15B (total EUR 7.05B-10.35B) must be assigned funded, deferred or cut. 1. Phase 1 definition and success test date (🔴 High)

Decision: Is Phase 1 defined as FID (Month 12 = 2027-10-17) to first-block energization (Months 42-48 = 2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17), with success tested at the Phase 2 FID, or kept as Months 12-36 (2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17) with energization inside it?

Why it is open: Pitch and executive summary say 500 MW energized in Months 12-36 (2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17). Canonical permitting and schedule say energization Months 42-48 (2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17) (downside 48-60), permit decisions Months 26-39 (2028-12-17 to 2030-01-17), ANSSI clearance Months 25-31 (2028-11-17 to 2029-05-17). Stabilization at Months 54-60 (2031-04-17 to 2031-10-17) falls outside the window.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Redefine Phase 1 as Month 12 (2027-10-17) FID to Months 42-48 (2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17) energization; Months 12-36 (2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17) is the construction-start window; test success at Phase 2 FID (about Months 54-60 = 2031-04-17 to 2031-10-17). Schedule becomes consistent with permits and ANSSI. Success is judged after 12 months of operating data. Permit-dependent works are conditional. phase_schedule_and_capacity, pitch, executive summary timeline, success definition wording.
B. Keep Months 12-36 (2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17) as a hard target and compress permits, ANSSI clearance and build. Needs fast-track status, which is not assumed. Build would start before permit decision and ANSSI clearance, so near-certain to miss. permitting_and_schedule_realism and ANSSI timeline would need unsupported assumptions.
C. Split into Phase 1a (permits and enabling works, Months 12-36 = 2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17) and Phase 1b (energization, Months 42-48 = 2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17). Clear milestones, but adds a gate and reporting layer. Tenant commitments must survive to Month 42 (2030-04-17). Roadmap, gate list, tenant term lengths.
  • If nobody decides: Documents keep contradicting each other; Month 12 (2027-10-17) gate and tenant terms are written against a window that cannot be met.

  • Decide by: Month 1 (2026-11-17), when the committee charter is set and before thresholds are locked at Month 2 (2026-12-17).

3. What the ~1 GW grid kill test ends (🔴 High)

Decision: Does failing the 'path to more than ~1 GW cumulative' test end only the 9 GW ambition (Phase 2+), or also Phase 1?

Why it is open: The ~1 GW test is the primary kill test, but the Phase 1 gate is only a 500 MW letter. A project can pass Month 12 (2027-10-17) with 500-999 MW and still meet the failure definition. A 750 MW downsize trigger appears in one review only. A shortfall leads to downsize, split, re-baseline or cancel, depending on the document.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Two separate tests: a 500 MW letter gates Phase 1; failing the >1 GW path ends Phase 2+ (single node or cancel). Phase 1 can proceed at 500-999 MW. The 9 GW ambition is explicitly ended on failure. Needs one consequence table. grid_kill_test, rte_phase1_gate, governance matrix.
B. Failing >1 GW path cancels the whole project. Strictest reading of the user's failure definition. Avoids stranded Phase 1 assets, but stops a viable 500 MW node. Kill criteria, Phase 1 gate.
C. Failure triggers a downsize to 250 MW with an early-warning level (for example 750 MW) as a proposed threshold. Preserves some option value. Adds a threshold with no source. curtailment_limits, Phase 1 base case, debt sizing.
  • If nobody decides: The Month 6 (2027-04-17) RTE letter is read only as a 500 MW test. The kill response is argued case by case, which invites sunk-cost override.
  • Owner: Gate Review and Kill Authority Committee, with sponsor and consortium
  • Decide by: Month 2 (2026-12-17), when numeric kill thresholds are locked, and before the Month 6 (2027-04-17) RTE letter.
  • Blocks: Month 6 (2027-04-17) RTE letter assessment and the Month 12 (2027-10-17) gate.

4. Phase 1 composition under a split campus (🟡 Medium)

Decision: If split campus is the default, is Phase 1 a fixed 500 MW total across nodes, or one 500 MW Cambrai node with the others deferred to Phase 2?

Why it is open: Canonical Phase 1 is 500 MW at one node (Cambrai/E-Valley). Nodes are listed as Cambrai 500 MW, Dunkirk 250 MW and Valenciennes 250 MW. The RTE tripwire of <500 MW per node cannot be met by a 250 MW node. The 30% tenant base, EUR 3B debt and EUR 10B ceiling depend on the answer.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Phase 1 is 500 MW in total, split across nodes (for example 250+250). RTE letters are needed per node, and the premium of EUR 250M-500M applies. Two sets of permits and land options. phase1_base_case, rte_phase1_gate, land and debt gates.
B. Phase 1 is a single 500 MW Cambrai node; other nodes are Phase 2 candidates. Simplest gates and the 150 MW tenant floor. Heavy dependence on one site and on RTE. topology_decision_rule, project goal.
C. Phase 1 is 250 MW at the lead node. About EUR 2.5B, delay 12-24 months. Lower risk, slower scale. Phase 1 size, debt target, tenant minimum (75 MW).
  • If nobody decides: Gates stay ambiguous; the Month 4 (2027-02-17) topology decision cannot set per-node RTE, tenant and debt tests.
  • Owner: Project Steering Committee, advised by the investment committee
  • Decide by: Month 4 (2027-02-17), at the topology decision, since the RTE letter and tenant floors depend on it.
  • Blocks: Month 4 (2027-02-17) topology lock; Month 6 (2027-04-17) RTE letter scope; Month 9 (2027-07-17) tenant gate.

Decision: Does the 70% option test apply to the Phase 1 node (about 900 ha) plus an expansion option, or to the full 161 km² square, and is the price ceiling 1.15x benchmark?

Why it is open: The gate is 70% at no more than 15% above benchmark. The full square is 16,100 ha (EUR 0.24B-0.40B). Review 14 prices relocation at 1.5-2.0x benchmark, which fails the gate and mixes 1.0x and 2.0x arithmetic.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Target parcel is the Phase 1 node plus an option on the expansion reserve; cost land at up to 1.15x. Achievable by Month 3-4 (2027-01-17 to 2027-02-17). Per-node land is about EUR 15.5M-25.9M (recomputed). 1.5-2.0x is the failure case that triggers the split. topology_decision_rule, land_option_gate, Review 14.
B. Target parcel is the full square. Almost certain to fail at Month 4 (2027-02-17), which forces the split. Land spend stays under EUR 60M before Month 4 (2027-02-17). land_option_gate.
C. Allow a higher premium (up to 2.0x) for Phase 1 land. Raises cost to EUR 45M per node and weakens the non-coercive claim. Risks community backlash. Land gate threshold, budget.
  • If nobody decides: The gate is run against the full square and fails at Month 4 (2027-02-17), so split campus follows by default.

6. Foreign equity versus the Month 12 (2027-10-17) equity-binding gate (🟡 Medium)

Decision: What share of the EUR 2.0B Phase 1 equity may be foreign, and who backstops it if it cannot be bound before ANSSI clearance?

Why it is open: Foreign co-investor equity cannot be bound at FID before clearance (about Months 25-31 = 2028-11-17 to 2029-05-17). The Month 12 (2027-10-17) gate requires equity sources bound. The investor profile includes sovereign-adjacent co-investors, and the foreign share is not stated.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Backstop with EU-domiciled non-controlling co-investors or sponsor equity. Equity can be bound at Month 12 (2027-10-17). Narrows the investor pool and may raise cost of capital. debt_financing_gate, investor structure.
B. Accept conditional foreign commitments at the gate, subject to ANSSI. Month 12 (2027-10-17) gate is conditional. Lenders may reject conditional equity, which risks the EUR 3B debt. Gate wording, financing terms.
C. Defer equity binding until clearance, so FID moves to about Month 24-30 (2028-10-17 to 2029-04-17). Tenant and lender commitments may lapse. Carrying costs rise. Phase 1 FID date, schedule.
  • If nobody decides: The Month 12 (2027-10-17) equity gate cannot be met by foreign capital, and FID is deferred or the gate is read as failed.
  • Owner: Steering Committee with consortium sponsors; ANSSI input via the Security Lead
  • Decide by: Month 6 (2027-04-17), when the informal ANSSI opinion is due and before lender conditions are written.

Stabilized volume is assumed at 100% of 500 MW contracted, with 85% average utilization for energy.

annual_opex_non_energy EUR 150M per year at 500 MW (about 3% of EUR 5B capex; includes staff EUR 20M–50M, maintenance, security, insurance, taxes) estimate The 3% ratio is an assumption (3% × 5,000 = 150). Staff cost range comes from the risk register (EUR 20M–50M annually in Phase 1). Scales to EUR 300M at 1 GW.
coverage_and_surplus Stabilized 500 MW: NOI EUR 400M (550−150), debt service EUR 299M, DSCR 1.34x, annual surplus before tax and distributions EUR 101M (about 5% of EUR 2.0B equity). Proposed lender minimum DSCR 1.30x. estimate Arithmetic: 400/299 = 1.34; 400−299 = 101; 101/2,000 = 5.1%. The chain closes only at the assumed price, 15-year tenor, 85% utilization with energy passed through, and no curtailment discounts; the 1.30x minimum is a proposed threshold.
coverage_stress_gap If tenants take a 10% lease discount for curtailment: revenue EUR 495M, NOI EUR 345M, DSCR 1.15x, gap about EUR 44M per year to reach 1.30x; fix by cutting debt to about EUR 2.66B (53% leverage) or an equity cure estimate Recomputed: 550×0.9 = 495; 495−150 = 345; 345/299 = 1.15; 1.30×299 = 389, 389−345 = 44; 345/1.30 = 265 debt service / 0.0996 = EUR 2.66B. The 5–15% discount range comes from the risk register.
energy_volume_and_price 500 MW at 85% average utilization = 425 MW average = 3.72 TWh per year; energy-only EUR 60/MWh (range 50–70, not verified) = about EUR 223M per year, passed through to tenants. Delivered cost (network tariffs, taxes) not yet established. estimate Recomputed: 425 MW × 8,760 h = 3.72 TWh; × EUR 60 = EUR 223M. EUR 50–70/MWh is an unverified energy-only assumption for nuclear-backed supply; delivered EUR/MWh must be validated in Phase 0 and is not the same figure.
energy_price_shock +EUR 30/MWh (e.g. 70 to 100) adds about EUR 112M per year at 500 MW and about EUR 2.0B per year at 9 GW (67 TWh). Without pass-through, 500 MW NOI falls to EUR 288M and DSCR to 0.96x. estimate Recomputed: 3.72 TWh × 30 = EUR 112M; 9,000 MW × 0.85 × 8,760 h = 67.0 TWh × 30 = EUR 2.0B; 400−112 = 288; 288/299 = 0.96. The review document's EUR 300M–600M per year at 9 GW is rejected as inconsistent with the volume. Index pass-through is therefore mandatory.
grid_kill_test Hosting capacity above about 1 GW (cumulative, any topology) is the primary kill test; uncontrolled until RTE signs a connection offer user constraint User failure definition. The risk register's 'firm 1 GW within 36 months' is not required at Phase 1 (see rte_phase1_gate), but if RTE gives no written path above 1 GW across nodes, the program is capped or downsized to 1 GW or less.
rte_phase1_gate RTE written preliminary feasibility letter for at least 500 MW within 36 months of the connection request, due by Month 6 (2027-04-17) (uncontrolled); firm connection offer for at least 500 MW targeted by Month 12 (2027-10-17) but unlikely, so a conditional pass is allowed proposed threshold Risk register and pre-project (Month 6 = 2027-04-17 letter) combined with the assumption that a firm offer within 12 months is unlikely. The tranche sequence 500 MW, 1 GW, 2 GW, 3 GW is put to RTE. Recomputed: a connection request filed in Months 1–3 (2026-11-17 to 2027-01-17) plus 36 months gives energization at the earliest about Months 37–39 (2029-11-17 to 2030-01-17) if RTE uses its full 36 months (the draft's Months 39–42 = 2030-01-17 to 2030-04-17 did not follow); the base case of Months 42–48 (2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17) allows for slippage. Either way this is after the end of the user's Phase 1 window (Month 36 = 2029-10-17). Failure triggers split-campus review or downsizing to 250 MW.
grid_reinforcement_exposure Developer co-funding of transmission reinforcement EUR 500M–1.5B (estimate); firm, no-flexibility connection adds EUR 200M–500M; at-risk RTE pre-engineering in Phase 0 EUR 50M–150M estimate Risk register and review document. On the 500 MW base (EUR 5B), co-funding fits under the EUR 10B ceiling (5.0+0.5 = EUR 5.5B to 5.0+1.5 = EUR 6.5B). On a 1 GW base (EUR 10B) it would breach the cap by EUR 0.5B–1.5B unless it is already included; this is unconfirmed. Pre-engineering is Phase 0 spend inside the EUR 750M cap, not Phase 1 capex.
curtailment_limits Target annual curtailment at most 10% (proposed), walk-away 15%; 30–90 days' notice; BESS 50–200 MWh; if above 15%, Phase 1 reduced to 500–750 MW or less proposed threshold The risk register proposes 10–15%, and the assumption and pre-project documents set 10% as target and 15% as ceiling. RTE's firm statement is due by Month 9 (2027-07-17) (uncontrolled). SLA 99.5–99.95% needs force-majeure carve-outs for RTE curtailment.
power_procurement_edf Blend of nuclear-linked contract, PPAs and BESS with index pass-through to tenants. EDF target: non-binding LOI for at least 500 MW, at least 10-year tenor, capped price by Month 6 (2027-04-17); term sheet by Month 9 (2027-07-17); binding contract not before FID. All uncontrolled until signed. decision Risk 3 (LOI at Month 6 = 2027-04-17) and the review document (Month 9 = 2027-07-17 term sheet or commitment by Month 18 = 2028-04-17) are merged. Multi-GW nuclear-backed supply is unconfirmed. Fallback if EDF declines: 250 MW first tranche on PPAs and spot/BESS. Sensitivities at +20%, +40% and +60% over baseline; the Phase 2 mothball price threshold is to be set in Phase 0.
topology_decision_rule Topology decision at Month 4 (2027-02-17). Single square only if at least 70% of its target parcel is optioned non-coercively AND RTE gives at least 1 GW to that node in writing; otherwise split campus (2–3 nodes of 250–500 MW). Because RTE's written letter is not due until Month 6 (2027-04-17), split campus is the default at Month 4 (2027-02-17) and the single square can be kept alive only if RTE written evidence is already in hand. Nodes: Cambrai/E-Valley 500 MW, Dunkirk 250 MW (range 250–500), Valenciennes/Denain/Escaudain 250 MW; Saint-Omer small satellite. proposed threshold Risk 13 and 19 and the pre-project advice give Month 4 (2027-02-17); the review's Month 3 (2027-01-17) decision date is rejected because land data is only first checked at Month 3 (2027-01-17). Sequencing conflict corrected: the draft required an RTE ≥1 GW confirmation at Month 4 (2027-02-17) although the RTE letter is due at Month 6 (2027-04-17), so the AND-condition cannot normally be met at Month 4 (2027-02-17). Nodes sum to 500+250+250 = 1,000 MW. Inter-node latency of 50 ms is rejected as too loose for tightly coupled training; tolerance is set from tenant data in Months 2–4 (2026-12-17 to 2027-02-17), and fiber adds about 1 ms RTT per 100 km (Cambrai–Dunkirk about 1.5 ms, estimate). Tightly coupled clusters stay within one node.
land_option_gate At least 70% of the chosen topology's target parcel under non-coercive option at no more than 15% above benchmark land value; first check Month 3 (2027-01-17), confirmed at Month 4 (2027-02-17) and the Month 12 (2027-10-17) gate (split nodes at least 80% optioned) proposed threshold Risk 2 and the review document. For a full single square 70% means about 113 km² (0.7×161 = 112.7), which is why failure is expected. Compulsory acquisition is not assumed and stays uncontrolled until a formal State decision exists. Conflict flagged, decision needed: the ≤15% premium test conflicts with the pre-project compensation basis of 1.5–2× benchmark (see ecology_and_farmland); the 15% test is kept for the gate and 1.5–2× is treated as a cost stress case.
land_use_and_hall_envelope Per 500 MW node about 8.9 km² (about 1.8 ha/MW at 161 km² per 9 GW). Built and hardstand area at most 30–50% of the envelope (estimate); the rest is buffers, ecology, farming, remediation zones. Halls 14–20 m tall (max 25–30 m), 20,000–100,000 m² each (some above 150,000 m²), 50–100+ buildings at 9 GW. estimate Recomputed: 161/9,000 = 0.0179 km²/MW = 1.79 ha/MW (the draft's 17.9 ha/MW was a factor-of-10 unit error); × 500 MW = 8.9 km² = about 890 ha. Hall dimensions are user constraints; 50–100 halls × about 60,000 m² gives only about 3–6 km² of roofs (2–4% of 161 km²), so the 30–50% built share is a ceiling covering substations, BESS, cooling yards and roads. Count check: 9 GW over 50–100 buildings implies 90–180 MW per building versus about 50–60 MW per hall in the Phase 1 base case (500 MW / 8–10 halls), so either halls grow or the count exceeds 100. Low-to-mid-rise is preferred because of floor loading, cooling and cabling, and fire/structural cost.
anchor_tenant_gate_phase1 Phase 0 gate: binding term sheets for at least 30% of Phase 1 size by Month 9 (2027-07-17), executed take-or-pay (or equivalent reservation agreement with fees paid) by Month 12 (2027-10-17). LOIs do not count. proposed threshold User rule on signed take-or-pay; 30% is the risk register and assumption threshold (300 MW of 1 GW, 150 MW of 500 MW). Phase 1 size is capped at signed MW ÷ 0.30; below a 250 MW viable minimum (0.30 × 250 = 75 MW signed) there is no Phase 1 FID. The 300 MW fixed figure applies only to the 1 GW case.
phase2_fid_gate Phase 2 FID requires signed take-or-pay for at least 50% of the next tranche (user floor 30–50%), at least 12 months of Phase 1 operating data, average PUE at most 1.28 across commissioned halls, power reliability and security/community targets met proposed threshold User states 30–50% of the next tranche; the choice of 50% for Phase 2 (stricter than Phase 1's 30% so the two gates differ, consistent with the review's 'at least 50% of Phase 2 demand'), the 12-month data period and the 1.28 PUE limit are proposals, so the kind is changed from user_constraint. Phase 2 FID cannot precede about Month 54–60 (2031-04-17 to 2031-10-17) in the base schedule (first-block energization Months 42–48 = 2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17 plus 12 months).
tenant_terms_and_credit Take-or-pay leases 5–10 years (proposed); reservation fee EUR 10M–50M per 100 MW, paid before construction and credited to rent (EUR 15M–75M at 150 MW); counterparty investment grade (BBB− or better) or parent guarantee/letter of credit proposed threshold Fee and tenor from the risk register; 1.5 × 10 = 15 and 1.5 × 50 = 75. The 'A−/BB+' minimum in the documents is internally inconsistent (BB+ is sub-investment grade) and is replaced with BBB−. Target mix: 2–3 hyperscalers/labs plus 2–3 sovereign or European anchors; each tenant 50–500 MW.
debt_financing_gate Firm debt commitment of at least EUR 3B for the 500 MW tranche, tenor at least 12 years, margin about benchmark +200 bps, by Month 12 (2027-10-17); equity sources bound for Phase 1 proposed threshold The risk register gives EUR 3B–5B; EUR 3B is chosen because it equals 60% of EUR 5B, and EUR 5B would exceed 60% leverage of a 500 MW tranche. Non-binding lender LOI by Month 9 (2027-07-17); lender engagement from Month 3 (2027-01-17). Spread +200–400 bps if evidence is weak. Consistency flag: at a 12-year tenor the 500 MW case gives DSCR 1.15x (see debt_terms_and_service), so the 12-year floor holds only with lower debt (about EUR 2.65B) or a 15-year target tenor; decision needed.
social_license_gate Written support from at least 2 of the 3 most affected municipalities by Month 12 (2027-10-17) (signatures targeted Month 9 = 2027-07-17), no major legal challenge pending; community-benefit package EUR 50M–150M over Phases 1–2 (estimate), contingent on permits proposed threshold Risk 12, pre-project and assumptions. Liaison committee Month 1–2, early voluntary consultation Month 3 (2027-01-17), formal 4-week consultation by Month 6 (2027-04-17), draft agreement Month 5 (2027-03-17). No binding local veto; a refusal by a key municipality triggers a reassessment. Jobs claims must reflect small operations headcount.
national_security_review Confidential ANSSI/DGSI pre-submission Months 0–1 (2026-10-17 to 2026-11-17); informal opinion Month 6 (2027-04-17); Month 12 (2027-10-17) written confirmation that formal review can start (Month 13 = 2027-11-17) with no blocking concern; formal clearance planned 12–18 months after the formal review starts (about Months 25–31 = 2028-11-17 to 2029-05-17), all uncontrolled proposed threshold Risk 11's 12–18 month target (review starting Month 13 = 2027-11-17: 13+12 = 25, 13+18 = 31) is used instead of the review's optimistic 6–12 months; the draft wording 'after start' is corrected to 'after formal review starts'. The review's Month 18 (2028-04-17) clearance is reframed as a Month 18 (2028-04-17) checkpoint (conditional letter or dated timeline). Security baseline campus-wide with hardened enclaves funded by sovereign tenants; Phase 0 security design EUR 5M–15M; Phase 1 security EUR 50M–200M (estimate).
permitting_and_schedule_realism Standard ICPE plus environmental authorization 18–30 months from filing (file submitted Month 8–9 = 2027-06-17 to 2027-07-17, decision about Months 26–39 = 2028-12-17 to 2030-01-17), appeals add 24–48 months; fast-track not assumed. First-block energization base case Months 42–48 (2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17); downside Months 48–60 (2030-10-17 to 2031-10-17). Permit check at Month 18 (2028-04-17). estimate Assumption document; the review's 'fast-track path assumed' is rejected as unconfirmed. Recomputed: filing Month 8 (2027-06-17) + 18 = Month 26 (2028-12-17) to Month 9 (2027-07-17) + 30 = Month 39 (2030-01-17) (the draft's Month 27 = 2029-01-17 start is corrected). The base case of Months 42–48 (2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17) holds only if the decision lands at the early end (about Months 26–30 = 2028-12-17 to 2029-04-17) and the first block takes about 12–18 months to build; a decision at Month 39 (2030-01-17) leaves only 3–9 months to Month 42–48 (2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17), so late permits fall into the downside case. This conflicts with the user's Phase 1 window of Months 12–36 (2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17): it can only be met if RTE and permits arrive early, which is uncontrolled. Pause drawdown if critical authorizations are not in formal examination by Month 18 (2028-04-17). One permit file per node.
cooling_pue_water_basis Closed-loop direct-to-chip with dry coolers, no evaporative water; PUE target 1.15–1.25. Phase 0: modelled PUE above 1.30 on a 35°C design day triggers design review; hot-weather PUE may reach 1.35–1.5 (estimate), peak grid load +5–15%. Written water-authority opinion by Month 6 (2027-04-17); expansion gate average PUE at most 1.28 user constraint PUE target and zero-water preference are user constraints. Thresholds 1.30 and 1.28 come from the risk register and assumptions. Tension flagged, decision needed: the risk register's own expected hot-weather PUE (1.35–1.5) exceeds the 1.30 design-day trigger, so the trigger would fire by default; it should be read as an annual-average or 30°C test (vendor guarantee PUE at most 1.25 at 30°C, penalty above 1.30) or the design-day limit reset. The Month 30 (2029-04-17) cooling gate is re-timed to 12 months after first-hall energization including one summer, since the base energization is after Month 30 (2029-04-17). Hydrological/thermal study (EUR 0.5M–1.2M) due Month 4 (2027-02-17); 2–5 MW pilot hall first.
immersion_and_heat_reuse Immersion pilot optional: starts at 10–50 MW with a dedicated tenant, scaling to 50–100 MW only if PUE at most 1.18 is validated; pilot failure risks EUR 50M–100M. Heat-reuse revenue = EUR 0 until a binding offtake is signed (infrastructure EUR 50M–200M at risk). decision User allows a 50–100 MW pilot; the risk register limits Phase 1 to 10–50 MW, so the pilot is staged to the user's range. Heat is unpriced upside per the strategic decision; heat infrastructure is built only as tenant- or offtaker-specific capex.
fiber_connectivity_gate At least 2 physically separate, audited routes (no shared duct, bridge or landing) to each of Paris, London, Brussels, Amsterdam and Frankfurt with at least 100 Tbps redundant capacity; written confirmation by Month 9 (2027-07-17); Marseille and subsea added by Phase 2; at least 2 independent UK landings and 2 FR/BE landings, any single landing carries at most 25% of cross-border capacity proposed threshold Risk 10 and 23 extended to the hubs the user lists. The draft's 'less than 25%' is corrected to 'at most 25%': four landings (2 UK + 2 FR/BE) at equal share each carry exactly 25%, so a strict <25% would need at least five landings. 'Fiber lit by Month 12 (2027-10-17)' is rejected because the first energization is Month 42 (2030-04-17) or later; fiber must be ready before it. Fallbacks: own/co-invested route 100–200 km (EUR 100M–500M) and subsea co-investment (EUR 300M–800M over Phases 1–2), both outside the base budget.
brownfield_liability_gate Phase I desktop assessments by Month 1 (2026-11-17); Phase II intrusive surveys by Month 3 (2027-01-17) on the top 2–3 sites per zone (EUR 1.5M–3M per zone); shortlist only parcels with remediation bounded to EUR 0–100M per site by Month 6 (2027-04-17); seller/public indemnity or escrow EUR 50M–250M; Phase 1 reserve EUR 100M–300M proposed threshold Risk 8 and pre-project. Late-found contamination EUR 100M–400M (estimate) could exceed the EUR 300M reserve at the top end; escalation above it triggers the FID gate. Survey cost over four zones is about EUR 6M–12M (4 × 1.5–3M), Phase 0 spend. The reserve is the 'remediation' line in the stacked add-ons and must not be counted again as separate contingency. Most contaminated zones are reserved for energy or restoration, not halls.
ecology_and_farmland Farmland displacement for the full square 10,000–15,000+ ha (estimate; Phase 1 node about 900 ha); land cost at EUR 15,000–25,000/ha for 16,100 ha = EUR 0.24B–0.40B; ecological compensation budget EUR 200M–300M (exposure up to EUR 500M); campus-wide ecological master plan by Month 6 (2027-04-17); DREAL screening opinion by Month 9 (2027-07-17) estimate Displacement and compensation from the risk and assumption documents; per-hectare prices are the pre-project proposal (1.5–2× benchmark, to be appraised, implying a benchmark of about EUR 10,000–12,500/ha). Recomputed: 16,100 ha × 15,000–25,000 = EUR 242M–403M, so land price is minor beside assembly risk. Conflict flagged, decision needed: 1.5–2× benchmark is a 50–100% premium, while land_option_gate allows at most 15% above benchmark; the prices here are an upper-bound cost stress, not what the option gate accepts. Compensation land competes with farmland; lease-and-continue farming is preferred.
usd_fx_policy Campus company holds zero unhedged USD; hardware EUR 1.5B–2.3B sits with tenants/lessor. Any developer-side forward is allowed only against signed take-or-pay, hedge ratio 0.5–1.0, cost 0.5–2% per year. 10% EUR/USD move = EUR 150M–230M. Planning rate 1.08–1.12 (not verified). decision Strategic decision 2 (separate vehicle) and risk 14. Recomputed: 10% × 1.5–2.3B = EUR 150M–230M; full-ratio hedge cost 0.5% × 1.5B = EUR 7.5M up to 2% × 2.3B = EUR 46M per year. Hardware bought before signed demand leaves FX and stranded-asset risk that derivatives do not remove.
governance_and_kill_authority Independent investment committee chartered at Month 1 (2026-11-17) (at least 2 external directors, lender/co-investor observers); numeric kill thresholds fixed in writing by Month 2 (2026-12-17); external red team (EUR 2M–5M) with monthly pass/fail opinions; override only by supermajority (proposed two-thirds) with dissent published to lenders decision Strategic decision 5 option 1, risk 4 (thresholds by Month 2 = 2026-12-17) and the review/pre-project (charter Month 1 = 2026-11-17). Pre-project's 'simple majority for continuation' is tightened: a breach triggers automatic review and continuation needs affirmative approval. Pre-permit commitment of Phase 1 capital is proposed at no more than 10% of Phase 1 capex (10% × EUR 5B = about EUR 500M at 500 MW) until final permits.
fallbacks_vs_budget_and_dates Split pivot after Phase 0: +EUR 250M–500M capex (5–10% of EUR 5B) +EUR 300M–600M carrying, +6–12 months, so energization Months 48–60 (2030-10-17 to 2031-10-17): fits the EUR 10B ceiling (EUR 5.55B–6.1B) but misses the Months 12–36 (2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17) window. Split from the start: Phase 0 +EUR 100M–250M, +3–6 months: breaches the EUR 750M cap by up to EUR 250M and Month 12 (2027-10-17) gate, needs a new funding decision. 250 MW downsize: about EUR 2.5B, delay 12–24 months, fits. Stacked contingent add-ons on 500 MW (grid co-funding, split premium, carrying, remediation, fiber, subsea): EUR 1.55B–4.2B, giving EUR 6.55B–9.2B, still under EUR 10B but overlapping and unfunded. On a 1 GW base any add-on breaches the cap. estimate Recomputed from risk 13, 19, 1, 8, 10, 23 figures: 0.5+0.25+0.3+0.1+0.1+0.3 = 1.55 and 1.5+0.5+0.6+0.3+0.5+0.8 = 4.2 (simple sum, possible double-counting of carrying cost, which also sits in the split pivot line); 5+1.55 = 6.55 and 5+4.2 = 9.2. Split pivot: 5+0.25+0.3 = 5.55 and 5+0.5+0.6 = 6.1; 250 MW × EUR 10M/MW = EUR 2.5B; energization 42–48 plus 6–12 months = Months 48–60 (2030-10-17 to 2031-10-17). The stack omits several cost lines, so 'under EUR 10B' does not hold at the top end once they are added (see phase1_ceiling_headroom_500mw). Carrying costs are not clearly inside the EUR 5B–10B range; this must be confirmed.
phase1_ceiling_headroom_500mw Headroom to the EUR 10B ceiling on the 500 MW base: EUR 5.0B (10−5), unfunded. Stacked add-ons of EUR 1.55B–4.2B leave EUR 3.45B–0.8B. Cost lines outside the stack (ecological compensation EUR 0.2B–0.3B, Phase 1 security EUR 0.05B–0.2B, community benefit EUR 0.05B–0.15B, firm no-flexibility connection EUR 0.2B–0.5B) add EUR 0.5B–1.15B if they sit outside the EUR 5B base, giving EUR 7.05B–10.35B in total and free headroom from EUR 2.95B down to −EUR 0.35B (possible breach at the top end). estimate Added to close a gap: recomputed 10−5 = 5.0; 5.0−1.55 = 3.45 and 5.0−4.2 = 0.8; extra lines 0.2+0.05+0.05+0.2 = 0.5 and 0.3+0.2+0.15+0.5 = 1.15; totals 5+1.55+0.5 = 7.05 and 5+4.2+1.15 = 10.35; headroom 5−2.05 = 2.95 and 5−5.35 = −0.35. The EUR 100M–300M remediation reserve is already the remediation line of the stack and is counted once. Whether these lines are inside the EUR 5B base is not confirmed (decision needed); wage inflation of 10–20% on capex (EUR 0.5B–1B at 500 MW) is a further unmodelled exposure.
phase0_milestone_calendar Month 0 (2026-10-17): RTE/DREAL/ANSSI dialogue opens; Month 1 (2026-11-17): committee charter, red team, grid audit, ESA, hydrology and fiber audits commissioned; Month 2 (2026-12-17): thresholds locked; Month 3 (2027-01-17): land check, Phase II surveys, consultation; Month 4 (2027-02-17): topology decision; Month 6 (2027-04-17): RTE letter, water opinion, ANSSI opinion, EDF LOI, ecology plan, parcel shortlist (first 180 days = Months 0–6 = 2026-10-17 to 2027-04-17); Month 9 (2027-07-17): tenant term sheets, DREAL opinion, fiber and curtailment confirmations, grid audit published; Month 12 (2027-10-17): gate decision Merged from the risk register, review document and pre-project action lists, resolving date conflicts (topology Month 4 = 2027-02-17; thresholds Month 2 = 2026-12-17). Items requiring RTE, ANSSI, DREAL, water authorities, EDF or municipalities are uncontrolled until a contract, permit, formal decision or signed term sheet exists. Sequencing note: the RTE letter (Month 6 = 2027-04-17) follows the topology decision (Month 4 = 2027-02-17).
staffing_and_workforce Phase 0 core team 40–60 (estimate) with offices in Cambrai and Dunkirk; Phase 1 operations 50–150 FTE (not verified); training academy EUR 10M–30M for 200–500 technicians over 3–5 years; trade wage inflation risk 20–40% estimate Assumption and risk documents. Local-share hiring targets (e.g. 50% regional construction labor) are only proposals; employment claims must stay modest because operations headcount is small relative to the capital deployed. Consistency flags: academy output (200–500) is 1.3–10× the Phase 1 operations headcount (50–150), so it must serve construction trades and other regional employers; and opex staff cost of EUR 20M–50M over 50–150 FTE implies about EUR 0.13M–1.0M per FTE, which suggests the figure includes contractors or security (not verified).

Focus and Context

A 9 GW, 161 km² notional AI campus in Hauts-de-France enters Phase 0 (Months 0–12 = 2026-10-17 to 2027-10-17) feasibility testing. RTE grid hosting capacity above ~1 GW is the primary kill test. Phase 0 is capped at EUR 750M with four milestone tranches; no committed Phase 1 capital (EUR 5B–10B) before Month 12 (2027-10-17) gate. The plan is explicitly stress-tested against likelihood of downsizing, splitting across nodes, delaying or cancelling.

Purpose and Goals

Complete Phase 0 feasibility within EUR 750M budget and 12-month timeline. Validate five critical gates: (1) RTE ≥500 MW within 36 months; (2) topology lock (single-square vs. split-campus) on ≥70% parcel optionability and RTE evidence; (3) binding anchor-tenant take-or-pay ≥30% of Phase 1 signed; (4) firm debt and equity commitments; (5) written municipal support ≥2 of 3 and no legal blockage. Success (user definition) = Phase 0 and Phase 1 completed within budget with credible tenants and a Phase 2 FID backed by signed anchor commitments; Month 12 (2027-10-17) is the Phase 1 FID gate. Phase 2 FID requires at least 50% signed take-or-pay, at least 12 months of Phase 1 operating data and PUE at most 1.28, so the earliest Phase 2 FID is about Months 54–60 (2031-04-17 to 2031-10-17). Failure = any major gate unmet, triggering downsize, split, delay or cancellation.

Key Deliverables and Outcomes

Phase 0 gate decision (Month 12 = 2027-10-17): pass/fail on grid, land assembly, tenants, financing and permitting evidence. If pass, Phase 1 FID authorized (500 MW at Cambrai or split-campus topology). Deliverables: RTE preliminary feasibility letter, parcel shortlist with 70%+ option coverage, binding anchor-tenant term sheets ≥150 MW, debt and equity commitments (EUR 3B+ senior, EUR 2B+ equity), ANSSI clearance pathway, municipal endorsements, DSCR forecast 1.34x base (proposed lender minimum 1.30x; 1.15x is the 10%-discount stress result).

Timeline and Budget

Phase 0 Months 0–12 (2026-10-17 to 2027-10-17), four tranches EUR 150/250/200/150M (cumulative caps 150/400/600/750M) = EUR 750M hard cap (no overspend). Topology decision Month 4 (2027-02-17); RTE letter, water opinion, ANSSI preliminary and DREAL screening by Month 6 (2027-04-17); anchor-tenant term sheets, fiber audit and municipal support by Month 9 (2027-07-17); gate review and FID decision Month 12 (2027-10-17). Phase 1 Months 12–36 (2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17) if gates pass; energization Months 42–48 (2030-04-17 to 2030-10-17).

Risks and Mitigations

Primary risk: RTE hosting capacity above 1 GW is uncontrolled until Month 6 (2027-04-17) written letter, but topology locks Month 4 (2027-02-17), forcing split-campus default by calendar. Mitigation: accelerate RTE interim estimate to Month 3 (2027-01-17); commission independent grid audit by Month 1 (2026-11-17). Secondary risk: anchor-tenant term sheets and the EDF LOI and term sheet depend on each other (Month 9 = 2027-07-17), creating deadlock. Mitigation: request an indicative EDF price range by Month 4 (2027-02-17) (a request, not a plan fact); EDF LOI at Month 6 (2027-04-17); term sheet at Month 9 (2027-07-17); binding contract at FID or later. Tertiary risk: stacked Phase 1 add-ons (EUR 1.55B–4.2B) consume EUR 10B ceiling headroom by Month 9 (2027-07-17). Mitigation: publish unified cost-stack reconciliation and lender funding approval by Month 9 (2027-07-17), locking scope (500 MW vs. 250 MW downsize).

Audience Tailoring

This executive summary addresses the investment committee, senior debt lenders (EUR 3B+ commitment), co-investors (EUR 2B+ equity), and decision-making authorities (RTE, DREAL, ANSSI, municipalities). The tone is skeptical and gate-driven, emphasizing uncontrolled external dependencies and legitimate downsize/pause/cancel outcomes, not promotional.

Action Orientation

Month 0 (2026-10-17): initiate RTE/DREAL/ANSSI pre-submission dialogue; file RTE pre-engineering request; commission independent grid audit, environmental baselines, hydrology and fiber audits. Month 1 (2026-11-17): charter investment committee (independent directors, supermajority override, lender tri-party binding agreement); appoint red-team lead; lock numeric kill thresholds by Month 2 (2026-12-17). Month 3 (2027-01-17): complete land fragmentation surveys and Phase II intrusive brownfield assessments; solicit RTE interim estimate. Month 4 (2027-02-17): topology decision (contiguous or split based on 70% optionability check). Month 6 (2027-04-17): obtain RTE preliminary letter, water-authority opinion, ANSSI informal opinion, EDF LOI. Month 9 (2027-07-17): close anchor-tenant term sheets ≥150 MW, publish cost reconciliation, obtain municipal signatures. Month 12 (2027-10-17): investment committee gate review and Phase 1 FID authorization or documented deferral/downsize.

Overall Takeaway

A 9 GW AI campus is feasible only through staged, evidence-gated proof: grid capacity, land assembly, credible tenants and social license. Phase 0 stress-tests the ~1 GW hosting and ~70% parcel thresholds. If RTE, land, tenants and financing all validate by Month 12 (2027-10-17), Phase 1 proceeds at 500 MW with a pathway to 1–3 GW. If any gate fails, legitimate outcomes include 250 MW downsize, multi-node split, 12–24 month delay, or outright cancellation. The plan protects EUR 5B–10B Phase 1 capital from sunk-cost override via independent gate authority and numeric kill criteria locked in writing.

Feedback

Strengthen the summary by: (1) explicitly naming the three candidate node sites (Cambrai, Dunkirk, Valenciennes) and quantifying the split-campus cost premium (EUR 250M–500M, 5–10% of Phase 1 base); (2) clarifying whether the EUR 10B Phase 1 ceiling includes or excludes USD hardware (EUR 1.5B–2.3B), resolving the open decision upfront; (3) detailing the three gate-failure scenarios with specific outcomes (grid <500 MW → 250 MW downsize; parcel <70% → split topology; tenants <30% → Phase 1 pause to Month 24 = 2028-10-17), showing consequences in revenue and return terms; (4) documenting the timeline inversion risk: topology locks Month 4 (2027-02-17) before RTE letter Month 6 (2027-04-17), keep topology at Month 4 (2027-02-17) with split campus as default, and request the RTE interim estimate and the audit's interim findings by Month 3 (2027-01-17); any move to Month 6.5 (2027-05-02) would be a separate committee decision, not a plan fact; (5) quantifying DSCR stress impact: 10% lease discount drops 500 MW DSCR to 1.15x (EUR 44M annual shortfall), EUR 30/MWh energy shock drops to 0.96x; adding a sensitivity table would show debt/equity/dilution tradeoffs. These additions would make the plan's feasibility boundaries explicit and actionable for lenders and investors.

Part 2: Supporting analysis

Persuasive elevator pitch.

AI Compute Campus: Hauts-de-France Sovereign Scale Initiative

Project Overview

A 500 MW AI compute campus in Hauts-de-France offers Europe a credible path to sovereign AI scale without speculation or stranded capital. The project is structured as a staged, gate-driven model that protects investors from sunk-cost momentum while enabling authorities and communities to make evidence-based decisions.

Phase 0 (Months 0–12 = 2026-10-17 to 2027-10-17) gates the 9 GW ambition on hard evidence: RTE hosting capacity, parcel assembly, signed anchor tenants, debt binding, and social license. Hosting capacity above ~1 GW (cumulative, any topology) is the primary kill test for the 9 GW ambition, while a written ≥500 MW RTE letter is the Phase 1 gate (conditional pass allowed). This feasibility phase commits EUR 750M (hard cap, planning range EUR 250M–750M) with no committed capital before the Phase 0 gate.

If Phase 0 passes, Phase 1 delivers 500 MW by Months 12–36 (2027-10-17 to 2029-10-17) with predictable economics: EUR 550M annual revenue, EUR 150M annual opex, 1.34x DSCR, and EUR 101M annual surplus on EUR 5B capex. The project positions the campus as a reindustrialization anchor for Hauts-de-France industrial heritage, creating jobs (40–60 Phase 0 FTE; 50–150+ Phase 1 operations) and establishing a benchmark for evidence-gated scaling across the EU.

Target Audience

The pitch addresses:

  • Private hyperscale developer and infrastructure-fund consortium (including sovereign-adjacent co-investors)
  • Senior debt lenders (EUR-denominated, investment-grade bias)
  • Equity co-investors (family offices, strategic industrial groups)
  • Hyperscaler and sovereign-AI anchor tenants
  • Decision-making authorities (RTE, DREAL, ANSSI, municipalities)
  • Project lenders and external red-team advisers

The project positions the developer as a feasibility partner, not a promoter, addressing acute skepticism that any 9 GW single-site campus will face.
